meta.title: The Note From the Seller
meta.skill_frame: Argument and evidence: a claim whose only source gains from it.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 6.00, 6.00 and 6.18 on the three parts (109, 109 and 105 words), 6.06 together. The load is a claim whose only source has an interest in the sale, so the reader has to track who wrote the note and what they stood to gain.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for argument_evidence 4.2, band 4.2, sequence 5. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A theater program note, written by the shop that sold the sound gear, calling the gear the clearest in the region.
source.avoided: No theater name, shop name, brand, price, or season.

session.difficulty_basis: The only support for the sound gear claim is a note written by the shop that sold and installed it, after a trial in an empty hall.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: The theater sent its members a note about the new sound gear in the hall. The note calls the gear the clearest in the region and says every seat will hear each word. At the bottom, it names the shop that sold and put in the gear, and that shop wrote the note. The theater's director added one sentence of thanks but no test of the sound. The note describes a trial in an empty hall, where the shop's own worker spoke into a microphone. No crowd had used the gear when the note was printed, and the note is handed out at the door before the first show.
passage.part_2: A shop that sells sound gear has a reason to praise it. That does not make the praise false. It does mean the note is not a report from a neutral source, because the same business that gains from the claim wrote it, and it gives no sound reading and no comment from anyone outside the shop. The empty hall also differs from a full one, where bodies soak up sound and the back rows sit far from the stage. The note's one trial cannot stand for a whole season of plays. The shop also chose the speaker positions in the hall, which can change what a listener hears.
passage.part_3: The claim may turn out to be true, but this note cannot show it. The shop gains from the sale, so its words are a pitch, not a test. A reader would need a sound reading taken by someone else, or reports from people who came to several shows. The director's thanks do not supply that. The question is not whether the shop is honest, but whether anyone with no stake has checked the result, and a note written by the seller is a poor witness for the seller's goods. A seller's praise is worth less than a stranger's test, even when both are honest.

items.prompt: What does the note call the new sound gear?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The clearest in the region, with every seat hearing each word.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The note calls the gear the clearest in the region and says every seat will hear each word.
tutor_only.tell: The note calls the gear the clearest in the region and says every seat will hear each word.
help: The sentence about the note's praise names the claim.
It names the region and the seats.
tutor_only.core_idea: The clearest in the region, with every seat hearing each word.
accept_ideas: the clearest in the region
the best sound in the region
every seat will hear each word
the clearest sound gear around
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

the company that installed it
the seller
the shop that put it in
tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case, punctuation, and minor spelling. Accept a meaning-preserving paraphrase.

if_they_say.when: the student says the theater director wrote it
if_they_say.ask: The director added one sentence. Who wrote the note itself?

items.prompt: Why does that make the note weaker as evidence?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The shop gains from the sale, so its words are not a neutral report.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The shop gains from the claim, so the note is not a report from a neutral source.
tutor_only.tell: The shop profits if the claim is believed, so the note is not independent.
help: The sentence about the business that gains carries the answer.
It names the interest behind the claim.
tutor_only.core_idea: Because the shop gains from the sale, so the note is not neutral.
accept_ideas: the shop gains from the sale
it is not a neutral source
the seller profits if people believe it
the writer has an interest
not_required: whether the gear is under warranty

if_they_say.when: the student says the shop must be lying
if_they_say.ask: An interest does not prove a lie. What kind of source does it make the note?

items.prompt: A member says the note proves the gear is best. What is wrong with that?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. It is the seller's pitch, from one trial in an empty hall, with no outside check.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The note is the seller's own praise, based on one trial in an empty hall, and no one outside the shop checked the result.
tutor_only.tell: The note is a seller's pitch, tested once in an empty hall, with no outside check.
help: The sentences about the empty hall and the shop's interest carry the answer.
They name the trial and the missing outside check.
tutor_only.core_idea: It is the seller's pitch, from one empty-hall trial, with no outside check.

one empty-hall trial proves little
no one outside the shop checked
the shop chose the speaker positions
not_required: whether the director liked the sound

if_they_say.when: the student says the note is false because the shop profits
if_they_say.ask: The note may be true. The problem is that the seller is the only witness.

tutor_only.tell: A measurement by someone outside the shop, or audience reports after several shows.
